newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end sharply higher on shekel rebound.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end sharply higher on shekel rebound.

text.p: Israeli shares surged on moderate volume on Tuesday as the shekel rebounded strongly against the dollar, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares ended up 1.87 percent, or 5.34 points, to 290.32 on all-share turnover of 151 million shekels against 112 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.27 percent higher at 298.73.

The shekel surged one percent against the dollar on Tuesday, reversing a five percent it took in the last week of June in the wake of a reform of the exchange rate regime and a sharp 1.2 percentage point cut in interest rates.

"The uncertainty in the forex market had a negative impact on the stock market. Now it seems that the shekel is stabilising and investors are gaining confidence," said Amir Eyal of Epsilon Securities.

"Usually the market dives when the shekel declines but today it had a paradoxical impact on trading. Investors were afraid that the shekel's decline would lead to higher inflation," said Michael Politzer, head of the economics department at Central Securities Corp.

"The market feared that a sharp decline of the shekel would eventually lead to an interest rate hike. Now the cloud is fading away and the market can return to the positive course," Eyal added. He noted that turnover continued to be restrained.
Politzer said the market's expected recovery would be aided by the new issues market. "The new wave of public offerings next month will help the market gain momentum," he said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which gained 0.75 percent to 549 agorot on turnover of 16.5 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.5 percent to 759 agorot on volume of 7.6 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which surged 4.0 percent to 440 agorot on turnover of 5.8 million shekels.
Lehman Brothers initiated coverage of Israel Chemicals on Tuesday rating it an "outperform". Lehman said the company should achieve earnings per share growth of 27 percent in the next three years.
